text:
olivia: Heads up — noticed a 6-8% tail latency regression on long-seq GQA runs after the kernel-picker change landed. Repro on perf-gpu-3 when seq_len > 1024 and batch size >= 4. @raj can you take a look? :eyes:

raj: Ugh. Which commit? any flame graphs or nvprof dumps?

olivia: The change is 9c4b2f7 — adds heuristic to prefer MQA kernels when per-head dim < 64 regardless of physical sharding. I ran a quick profile and attached the hotspots below. Looks like paged-kv slab copying increased and a few kernels hit lower SM occupancy.

olivia: Profiling snippet:
```
# perf summary (condensed)
Model: gqa-16b, inputs: seq=1536, batch=4
Time breakdown:
  exec kernels: 72.4%
  kv slab copy: 12.1%  <-- up from 4.2% baseline
  reduce + reorder: 8.3%
Hot kernels:
  gqa_attention_paginated_kernel (selected MQA variant)  41.2%
  kv_page_manager_copy  12.1%
  qkv_matmul_mqa_shard  9.6%
GPU occupancy: avg SM% 64 -> baseline 82
```

mike: Interesting. So the picker prefers MQA kernel which uses smaller per-shard GEMMs but ends up fragmenting KV pages? Could be that our MQA kernel assumes contiguous KV layout, but paged layout causes extra memcopies.

anya: If MQA picks reduce per-thread registers or warps, that can drop occupancy when seq is high. Maybe picker should be seq-aware: prefer GQA when seq_len * batch exceeds a threshold, even if per-head < 64.

raj: Agreed. I dug into the kernel metadata: the chosen MQA kernel declares lower register usage but higher shared mem for page buffering. With large seq it triggers extra page copies to keep per-shard KV contiguous. I can reproduce locally with the micro-bench.

raj: Quick test patch: add seq_threshold parameter to kernel_selector config and fallback to GQA when seq_len >= seq_threshold. Patch diff:
```diff
- selector.prefers_mqa = per_head_dim < 64
+ selector.prefers_mqa = per_head_dim < 64 && seq_len < selector.seq_threshold
```

olivia: Nice. What value do you propose for seq_threshold? 1024? 2048? We saw regression at 1536.

mike: Start conservative: 1280 might avoid flips at 1536 but keeps wins at smaller sizes. But better to compute based on estimated KV pages: pages = ceil(seq_len / page_block). If pages > 2 then prefer GQA. That ties to block size config.

anya: +1 to page-aware rule. We already expose page_block in paged-kv config. Suggest selector rule pseudocode:
```
pages = ceil(seq_len / cfg.page_block)
if pages >= cfg.page_count_threshold: choose GQA
else if per_head < cfg.mqa_head_dim_thresh: choose MQA
```
where cfg.page_count_threshold=3 default.

perfbot: CI perf-checker: job perf/gpu/longseq/1536x4 failed threshold (+7.2% p99 latency). See https://ci.re/redwood/perf/18812 for traces.

olivia: Good catch perfbot. @raj can you prototype the page_count_threshold patch and run the microbench across seq=[512,1024,1536,2048] with both page_block=512 and 256? Also include sm-occupancy in output.

raj: On it. I'll push a branch 'picker-pageaware-18812' with tests. Expect results by EOD.

mike: If that works, we should also add a lightweight runtime metric and alert when picker flips frequently for a customer — flipping can create perf jitter.

anya: Also add unit tests to validate that when page_count >=3 we prefer GQA even if per_head=32. Keeps semantics stable.

olivia: Thanks team. Follow-ups:
- raj: prototype + microbench (EOD)
- mike: add alert proposal PR
- anya: unit test snippets + config defaults PR
I'll file a perf regression incident with the trace and tag the deploy that rolled the picker change. :+1:

perfbot: Incident filed: PERF-18812 (linked). CI snapshots attached.

raj: quick note — initial microbench shows that switching to page-aware rule restores baseline p99 for 1536 and doesn't regress 512/1024. Will post numbers in branch.

olivia: Awesome, please paste the numbers here when ready and include flame graphs. Thanks! :shipit:
